question: A directed line through the point $A(1,-1,2)$ has direction cosines $\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},-\frac{2}{3}$ and meets the plane $x+y+z=3$ at $B$. Determine the coordinates of $B$ and hence use the points $A$ and $B$ to verify the direction cosines, obtain a suitable set of direction ratios, and write the vector and Cartesian equations of the line.
explanation:
Formation of the Line
Since the direction cosines are $\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},-\frac{2}{3}$, a point on the directed line through $A(1,-1,2)$ can be written as
$$x=1+\frac{2t}{3},\quad y=-1+\frac{t}{3},\quad z=2-\frac{2t}{3}$$
The point $B$ also lies on the plane $x+y+z=3$. Therefore,
$$1+\frac{2t}{3}-1+\frac{t}{3}+2-\frac{2t}{3}=3$$
$$2+\frac{t}{3}=3$$
Hence, $t=3$. Substituting this value gives
$$B=(3,0,0)$$

Verification of Direction Cosines
The direction ratios of the directed line from $A$ to $B$ are
$$3-1,\quad 0-(-1),\quad 0-2$$
that is,
$$2,1,-2$$
Also,
$$AB=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+(-2)^2}=3$$
Hence, the direction cosines obtained from the two points are
$$\frac{2}{3},\quad \frac{1}{3},\quad -\frac{2}{3}$$
which agree with the given direction cosines.

Formation of Equations
A vector parallel to the line is $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. Hence the vector equation is
$$\vec{r}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$$
Equating components,
$$x=1+2\lambda,\quad y=-1+\lambda,\quad z=2-2\lambda$$
Therefore, the Cartesian equation is
$$\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{1}=\frac{z-2}{-2}$$

Final Result
The point of intersection is $B(3,0,0)$, a suitable set of direction ratios is $2,1,-2$, the verified direction cosines are $\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},-\frac{2}{3}$, and the required vector and Cartesian equations are $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ and $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{1}=\frac{z-2}{-2}$ respectively.

options.A: $B=(3,0,0)$; direction ratios $(2,-1,-2)$; $\vec r=(\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-\hat j-2\hat k)$
options.B: $B=(3,0,0)$; direction ratios $(2,1,-2)$; direction cosines $\left(\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},-\frac{2}{3}\right)$; $\vec r=(\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)$; $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{1}=\frac{z-2}{-2}$
options.C: $B=(2,0,1)$; direction ratios $(1,1,-1)$; $\vec r=(\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i+\hat j-\hat k)$
